Associated Paper: Roth et al., "DeepOrgan: Multi-level Deep Convolutional Networks for Automated Pancreas Segmentation," MICCAI 2015
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: No capsule; draped across/behind stomach and duodenum; shape/position/volume shift with respiration, gastric/duodenal filling, peristalsis, patient positioning, and pathology
Benchmark Usage: Basis for DeepOrgan and nearly every subsequent pancreas CNN/transformer segmentation paper

Dataset: BTCV (Multi-Atlas Labeling Beyond the Cranial Vault)
Anatomy: 13 abdominal organs (spleen, kidneys, gallbladder, esophagus, liver, stomach, aorta, IVC, portal/splenic veins, pancreas, adrenal glands)
Associated Paper: Landman et al., "2015 MICCAI Multi-Atlas Labeling Beyond the Cranial Vault – Workshop and Challenge"
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Stomach distends/empties; bowel/vasculature pulse and shift with respiration/peristalsis; pancreas/adrenals are soft and positionally variable; large inter-patient variability
Benchmark Usage: Used to evaluate TransUNet, Swin-UNet, nnU-Net, and most abdominal segmentation foundation models

Annotation: Liver parenchyma, vessel tree, tumor masks
Associated Paper: IRCAD research dataset description (no single peer-reviewed introduction paper)
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Compresses/expands with respiration; displaced by diaphragm motion and adjacent-organ contact; shape distorted by tumor growth and surgical planning scenarios
Benchmark Usage: Standard cross-validation benchmark for liver/vessel segmentation, often paired with SLIVER07

Associated Paper: Heimann et al., "Comparison and Evaluation of Methods for Liver Segmentation From CT Datasets," IEEE TMI, 2009
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Respiration-driven displacement; compression against neighboring organs; shape/density variability across disease states (cirrhosis, tumors)
Benchmark Usage: The original MICCAI liver segmentation grand challenge; still a standard comparison point

Associated Paper: Antonelli et al., "The Medical Segmentation Decathlon," Nature Communications, 2022
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Respiration + tumor growth/regression over time; shape varies with disease state (cirrhotic distortion)
Benchmark Usage: Core MSD task; used in nnU-Net, SegVol, universal segmentation model evaluations

Associated Paper: Antonelli et al., "The Medical Segmentation Decathlon," Nature Communications, 2022
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Same pancreatic deformability as NIH Pancreas-CT, plus tumor-driven mass effect and growth/shrinkage across treatment timepoints
Benchmark Usage: Standard pancreas+tumor benchmark; used in nnU-Net and transformer-based abdominal segmentation papers

Associated Paper: Antonelli et al., "The Medical Segmentation Decathlon," Nature Communications, 2022
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Vascular displacement/compression from tumor mass effect, blood-flow/pressure changes, respiration
Benchmark Usage: Used in nnU-Net benchmark suite and vascular/tumor segmentation robustness studies

Associated Paper: Antonelli et al., "The Medical Segmentation Decathlon," Nature Communications, 2022
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Volume/shape change with disease (splenomegaly); shifts position with respiration and adjacent organ filling
Benchmark Usage: One of the most-used small-sample segmentation tasks for benchmarking new architectures

Associated Paper: Antonelli et al., "The Medical Segmentation Decathlon," Nature Communications, 2022
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Peristalsis, gas/fecal distension, bowel filling continuously change shape/length/position; tumor mass effect and luminal narrowing
Benchmark Usage: Used in MSD suite and colon-cancer segmentation robustness papers

Associated Paper: Roth et al., "A new 2.5D representation for lymph node detection using random sets of deep convolutional neural network observations," MICCAI 2014
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Disease-driven size/shape change; displaced by vascular pulsation and respiration; highly variable position/morphology
Benchmark Usage: Underpins Roth et al. (2014) CADe detection and Seff et al. (2015) segmentation benchmarks

Associated Paper: Heller et al., "The KiTS19 Challenge Data: 300 Kidney Tumor Cases with Clinical Context, CT Semantic Segmentations, and Surgical Outcomes," 2019
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Shifts with respiration; displaced/deformed by exophytic tumor growth, distorting renal contour
Benchmark Usage: Major MICCAI 2019 challenge; widely used to benchmark 3D U-Net variants

Annotation: Expert organ-at-risk contours on both timepoints
Associated Paper: Hong et al., "CT and cone-beam CT of ablative radiation therapy for pancreatic cancer with expert organ-at-risk contours"
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Pairs pre-treatment planning CT with same-patient CBCT during ablative radiotherapy, capturing real deformation from positioning, breath-hold variability, and treatment-related tissue change
Benchmark Usage: Purpose-built benchmark for CT-to-CBCT deformable registration/auto-segmentation in radiotherapy

Dataset: Abdominal CT Vessel Bifurcation Landmark Pair Dataset
Annotation: Manually identified paired anatomical landmarks across two CT volumes
Associated Paper: Criscuolo et al., "A Vessel Bifurcation Landmark Pair Dataset for Abdominal CT Deformable Image Registration (DIR) Validation," 2025
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Landmarks at vessel bifurcations capture real respiration-, positioning-, and filling-driven abdominal vasculature shift, explicit, quantified ground truth
Benchmark Usage: First abdominal counterpart to the long-standing DIR-Lab lung landmark benchmark

Dataset: Liver CT Vessel Bifurcation Landmark Pair Dataset
Associated Paper: Criscuolo et al., "A comprehensive liver CT landmark pair dataset for evaluating deformable image registration algorithms," 2024
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Landmarks directly quantify liver displacement/shape change between timepoints, driven by respiration and positioning
Benchmark Usage: Reference benchmark for liver-specific DIR algorithms used in SBRT/liver radiotherapy planning

Dataset: Gibson et al. 90-Case Abdominal Multi-Organ CT
Anatomy: 8 abdominal organs (spleen, kidney, gallbladder, esophagus, liver, stomach, pancreas, duodenum)
Annotation: Dense voxel-wise reference segmentations for all 8 organs
Associated Paper: Gibson et al., "Automatic Multi-Organ Segmentation on Abdominal CT with Dense V-Networks," IEEE TMI, 2018
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Adds gallbladder (bile filling/emptying), esophagus (swallowing/peristalsis), duodenum (gastric emptying/peristalsis) to BTCV's deformable-organ set
Benchmark Usage: Dense V-Networks reference standard, reused as an extension of BTCV/Pancreas-CT in later papers

Associated Paper: TCIA collection description; see TCIA wiki for citation details
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Small, soft gland further distorted by tumor growth, mass effect, irregular tumor-gland boundaries, pre-/post-resection change
Benchmark Usage: Recognized small-sample TCIA oncology benchmark for adrenal tumor segmentation/classification

Anatomy: Tissue sections, lung lobes, mammary gland, lesions
Annotation: Manually placed corresponding landmarks across consecutive stained sections
Associated Paper: Borovec et al., "ANHIR: Automatic Non-Rigid Histological Image Registration Challenge," IEEE TMI, 2020
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Each tissue section is cut/mounted/stained separately, causing real non-linear mechanical deformation between consecutive slices of the same tissue block
Benchmark Usage: Standard reference for histological registration comparison (BIRL framework); ISBI 2019 challenge

Dataset: ACROBAT (Automatic Registration Of Breast Cancer Tissue)
Associated Paper: Weitz et al., "The ACROBAT 2022 Challenge: Automatic Registration Of Breast Cancer Tissue," Medical Image Analysis, 2024
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Same mechanical-deformation mechanism as ANHIR, at larger scale across more stain types
Benchmark Usage: Largest WSI-registration benchmark; still niche outside digital pathology registration

Dataset: SCARED (Stereo Correspondence and Reconstruction of Endoscopic Data)
Annotation: Structured-light ground-truth depth maps per keyframe
Associated Paper: Allan et al., "Stereo Correspondence and Reconstruction of Endoscopic Data Challenge," 2021
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Organ surfaces continuously deform during live surgery from respiration, insufflation pressure, instrument contact
Benchmark Usage: MICCAI 2019 EndoVis sub-challenge; recognized in surgical computer vision

Associated Paper: Mountney, Stoyanov & Yang, "Three-Dimensional Tissue Deformation Recovery and Tracking," IEEE Signal Processing Magazine, 2010
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Tissue deformation plus rapid endoscope motion; gut wall contracts continuously
Benchmark Usage: Long-standing surgical/endoscopic vision reference; predates Kvasir-SEG-style sets

Dataset: SurgT (Soft-Tissue Tracking for Robotic Surgery Challenge)
Anatomy: Soft tissue surfaces in robotic surgery
Associated Paper: Cartucho et al., "SurgT challenge: Benchmark of Soft-Tissue Trackers for Robotic Surgery," Medical Image Analysis, 2024
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Real intraoperative soft-tissue deformation: breathing, heartbeat transmission, instrument manipulation
Benchmark Usage: First standardized soft-tissue tracking benchmark; unfamiliar outside surgical robotics

Dataset: FetReg2021 (Placental Vessel Segmentation & Registration in Fetoscopy)
Annotation: Pixel-wise class masks + registration ground truth
Associated Paper: Bano et al., "FetReg2021: A Challenge on Placental Vessel Segmentation and Registration in Fetoscopy," 2021
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Placental surface/vessel layout shifts with amniotic fluid movement, fetoscope motion, and laser-ablation treatment
Benchmark Usage: MICCAI 2021 EndoVis sub-challenge; specialized fetal-surgery benchmark

Dataset: USC-TIMIT / USC Speech & Vocal Tract MRI Database
Modality: Real-time MRI (rtMRI) + audio; volumetric static MRI
Task: Articulatory motion analysis, vocal-tract contour segmentation
Associated Paper: Narayanan et al., "Real-time magnetic resonance imaging and electromagnetic articulography database for speech production research," J. Acoustical Society of America, 2014
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Tongue/soft tissue deforms continuously (tens of times/sec) during speech via muscular contraction, an extreme fast-timescale deformation case
Benchmark Usage: Standard benchmark in speech-production/articulatory-phonetics research; unknown in mainstream segmentation research

Modality: Tagged cine MRI + SSFP cine MRI + 3D ultrasound
Annotation: 12 manually tracked landmarks across cardiac cycle
Associated Paper: Tobon-Gomez et al., "Benchmarking framework for myocardial tracking and deformation algorithms: an open access database," Medical Image Analysis, 2013
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Tagged MRI visualizes a grid that physically deforms with each heartbeat, literal, trackable tissue deformation
Benchmark Usage: Open STACOM benchmark hosted by Cardiac Atlas Project; foundational in cardiac strain-imaging

Annotation: Per-frame depth, surface normals, occlusion, optical flow, 6-DoF camera pose
Associated Paper: Bobrow et al., "Colonoscopy 3D Video Dataset with Paired Depth from 2D-3D Registration," Medical Image Analysis, 2023
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Deformable silicone phantoms mimic peristalsis, scope-induced stretching, luminal collapse; v2 has a dedicated deformation subset
Benchmark Usage: First dataset with genuine (non-simulated) ground-truth 3D geometry for colonoscopy depth/reconstruction

Dataset: HMC-QU (Hamad Medical Corporation–Qatar University Echocardiography Dataset)
Annotation: LV wall masks + segment-level MI/non-MI labels
Associated Paper: Degerli et al., "Early Detection of Myocardial Infarction in Low-Quality Echocardiography," IEEE Access, 2021
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: LV wall contracts/relaxes every heartbeat; MI causes specific segments to lose contractile motion (akinesis/hypokinesis), the deformation pattern itself is the diagnostic signal
Benchmark Usage: First public echocardiography dataset built for MI detection via wall-motion analysis

Dataset: Ultrasound Elastography Deformation Phantom Dataset (ÉTS Montréal)
Annotation: B-mode images + RF signals + ground-truth indentation/force/elastic-modulus parameters
Associated Paper: Dahmani, Petit & Laporte, "Ultrasound imaging dataset for elastography, deformation correction, and algorithm evaluation," SPIE Medical Imaging, 2025
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Robotic arm applies precisely measured, gradually increasing external compression, direct "external compression/mechanical forces" deformation with ground-truth values
Benchmark Usage: Purpose-built controlled-condition benchmark for elastography/deformation-correction algorithms

Associated Paper: Gómez et al., "BAGLS, a multihospital Benchmark for Automatic Glottis Segmentation," Scientific Data, 2020
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Vocal folds oscillate 100-300+ times/sec during phonation; further distorted by disease (paresis, edema, papilloma, granuloma)
Benchmark Usage: First public multihospital glottis-segmentation benchmark; standard in computational laryngology

Annotation: Instance-level masks for bolus, pharynx, larynx
Associated Paper: Zeng et al., "Video-TransUNet: Temporally Blended Vision Transformer for CT VFSS Instance Segmentation," ICMV 2022
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Pharynx/larynx/esophagus sequentially contract, elevate, and reshape within ~1 second during swallowing
Benchmark Usage: Newly released dysphagia-assessment benchmark; rare public fluoroscopic swallowing data

Annotation: Pixel-level masks for 4 structures + FIGO-type labels
Associated Paper: Pan et al., "Large-scale uterine myoma MRI dataset covering all FIGO types with pixel-level annotations," Scientific Data, 2024
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Shape/wall thickness/cavity volume change with menstrual cycle, pregnancy history, and fibroid growth (asymmetric, FIGO-dependent distortion)
Benchmark Usage: Largest public uterine-MRI segmentation dataset to date (2024)

Associated Paper: Meiburger et al., "Carotid Ultrasound Boundary Study (CUBS): an open multi-center analysis of computerized intima-media thickness measurement systems and their clinical impact," Ultrasound in Medicine & Biology, 2021
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Continuous cyclic wall motion with every heartbeat, plus slow disease-driven thickness/stiffness change (atherosclerosis)
Benchmark Usage: Long-standing multi-center reference for IMT algorithm comparison in vascular ultrasound

Associated Paper: Leitner et al., "A Human-Centered Machine-Learning Approach for Muscle-Tendon Junction Tracking in Ultrasound Images," IEEE TBME
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Junction physically slides/shifts by centimeters during muscle contraction; sliding behavior differs between healthy and impaired subjects
Benchmark Usage: Dedicated biomechanics/sports-medicine tracking benchmark with public leaderboard

Dataset: Fasted-State Gastric Antral Motility MRI + Manometry Dataset (Univ. of Nottingham)
Annotation: MRI-derived contraction measurements + manometric pressure ground truth
Associated Paper: Heissam et al., "Measurement of fasted state gastric antral motility... Validation of MRI method against concomitant perfused manometry in healthy participants," PLOS ONE, 2020
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Rhythmic antral wall contractions (peristalsis) physically propel/mix stomach contents; validated against a gold-standard pressure-sensor reference
Benchmark Usage: Methods-validation reference for gastric motility MRI vs. manometry

Associated Paper: Chen, Bai, Ou, Lu & Wang, "PSFHS: Intrapartum ultrasound image dataset for AI-based segmentation of pubic symphysis and fetal head," Scientific Data, 2024
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Pubic symphysis widens as relaxin softens its ligaments during labor, while the fetal head simultaneously molds and descends, two structures deforming together, with their relative position as the clinical target
Benchmark Usage: Basis of MICCAI 2023 PS-FH-AOP challenge; largest public intrapartum ultrasound segmentation benchmark

Number of Cases/Images: 5,000+ image pairs (100 with full landmarks + masks)
Associated Paper: Krasnova et al., "MGRegBench: A Novel Benchmark Dataset with Anatomical Landmarks for Mammography Image Registration," 2025
Why the Anatomy Is Deformable: Each mammographic view compresses/reshapes the breast differently; registering across views/sessions requires modeling tissue deformation under variable external compression
Benchmark Usage: Brand-new (Dec 2025) benchmark for a problem normally handled with ad hoc internal datasets
